Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

quality noun

how good something is

also good quality, high quality, high-quality, top quality, poor quality, first-rate, second-rate

classical

Phaedr. 4.9.8: tanta bonitās est aquae
Plin. NH 18.105: siliginis bonitāte
Cic. Rosc. Am. 20: bonitās praediōrum (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 323

bonitās, bonitātis f.

noun, third declension

good quality, goodness (of a thing)

Of land, water, wine and goods as well as of people. Pliny grades it: secunda bonitās, the second quality (NH 12.48, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • virtūs, virtūtis f. — worth, quality (of a thing as well as a person)

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 728: prō virtūte ut vēneat; Cic. Leg. 1.45: nec arboris nec equī virtūs (Lewis & Short)

    The opposite is vitium, a fault: so in Plautus, of goods on the market.

  • nota, notae f. — a grade, the quality of goods

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Brut. 287: hae notae sunt optimae, of wines; Col. 9.15.3: secundae notae mel (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. quality: high-quality, first-rate; quality: second-rate

    From the mark on a wine jar that showed its vintage; Morgan–Owens gives prīmae or optimae notae for first-rate, secundae notae for second-rate.

Examples

  • dēscende, amīce; tanta bonitās est aquae, voluptās ut satiārī nōn possit mea

    come down, friend: the water is so good that I can’t drink my fillPhaedr. 4.9.8–9

  • quae probast mers, pretium eī statuit, prō virtūte ut vēneat

    goods that are good he prices so that they sell for what they are worthPlaut. Mil. 728

  • atquī hae notae sunt optimae

    and yet these vintages are the bestCic. Brut. 287

See also quality, goods, quality assurance.
